**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 24</mark>**<sup>**th**</sup> **<mark>August 2010</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for May 2010** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for May 2010 world copper supply and demand in its August 2010 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for May 2010 indicated a production deficit of 93,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, May showed a deficit of about 37,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first five months of 2010, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 190,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 46,000 t). This compares with a production surplus of around 8,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 223,000 t) for the same period in 2009. 

World refined copper usage in May 2010 grew by 7.4% compared with that in May 2009, mainly owing to the continued recovery from 2009 weak usage levels in Japan, the European Union (EU), and the United States and to a 5% increase in Chinese apparent usage. During the first 5 months of 2010, world apparent usage grew by 8.4% (620,000 t) compared with that in the first 5 months of 2009. Usage grew by 3.6% in China, 11.5% in the EU, 37% in Japan and 4.5% in the United States.  Combined, these four regions currently account for 71% of total world refined copper usage. 

Despite capacity increases, world mine production in the first five months of 2010 remained practically unchanged compared with that in the same period of 2009 (+0.3%).  Furthermore, when compared with production in the first 5 month of 2008 (before temporary closures/production cuts occurred), world mine production declined by 2.4%. Production in Chile, the leading world producer that accounted for 33% of 2009 global production, was up slightly (1.8%), but output from Peru, the United States, Australia and Indonesia, which combined accounted for about 27% of 2009 global production, decreased by an aggregated 7.5%.  Mine production capacity utilization rates in the first 5 months of 2010 declined to about 77.5%. 

During the first 5 months of 2010, world refined production increased by 5.7% (420,000 t) compared with production in the same period of 2009: primary production increased by 2.2%, while secondary production (from scrap) increased by 27%. Note that the large relative increase in secondary refined copper production reflects in part the lower copper prices and consequent tight scrap market that existed in early 2009. World growth has been mainly driven by China (15.5%), Japan (13%) and the EU (8.8%) that combined represent almost one half of world refined copper production. Production in two other major world producers, Chile and the United States, which account for about one quarter of world production, decreased by a combined 2.5%. The ref

ined production capacity utilization rate in the first five months of 2010 increased to almost 80% from 77% in the same period of 2009 and reflects increased scrap availability and the restoration of temporary cuts made in early 2009. The average LME cash price for July 2010 was US$ 6,735.25 per tonne, up from the June 2010 average of US$ 6,499.30 per tonne. The 2010 high and low copper prices through the end of July were US$7,950.50 and US$6,091.00 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$7,070.62 per tonne. As of the end of July 2010, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 608,960 t, a decrease of 78,731 t from stocks held at the end of December 2009.
